QUOTE: "**Everywhere else** (applications and integrators), the default applies and direct member access is a compile error unless they define the macro themselves before including the headers." and "The define is turned on in three places... `library/common.h`... `programs/ssl/ssl_client2.c`..."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that code defining the opt-out (the library and the ssl programs) gets plain member names, while ordinary consumers of the public headers get the renamed `private_` members.
